description: 5 exemplars (1 de) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Exemplars follow the description and When-to-use: a shared Sentry URL, 'check Sentry', error-pattern and affected-user analysis, adding breadcrumbs, and release tracking. Near-misses share the production-error vocabulary and route elsewhere: a proactive bug hunt with no Sentry signal (bug-analyzer), deciding which alerts page on-call (alerting-doctrine), and establishing which observability signals exist at all (logging-monitoring). Counterexamples guard the 'sentry' homonym and unrelated test work.

queries.q: https://sentry.io/organizations/acme/issues/4821/ — what's going on with this one?
check Sentry for new unresolved errors in production since the last release
how many users are hit by the checkout TypeError, and which browsers does it come from?
add Sentry breadcrumbs around the payment webhook handler so we can see what happened before the crash
schau mal in Sentry, warum der Export-Job seit dem Deploy heute Nacht ständig abbricht
audit the order service for hidden bugs before we release it
queries.note: proactive bug hunting with no Sentry signal to investigate → bug-analyzer

queries.q: which of our production alerts should actually page the on-call engineer?
queries.note: production-alert vocabulary, but the question is the paging doctrine, provider-neutral → alerting-doctrine

queries.q: what observability do we actually have — which of the four golden signals are instrumented?
queries.note: establishing the signal inventory rather than investigating an error in one tool → logging-monitoring

queries.q: write the sentry rotation schedule for the night guards at the warehouse
queries.note: the 'sentry' homonym — a guard post, not the error tracker

queries.q: write a unit test for the date formatter
queries.note: routine test work with no production error involved
